note: corners are [RA_deg, Dec_deg] in JPEG raster order: TL, TR, BR, BL

images.label: NGC 55 Whale / Pearls
images.distance_note: Tip of the red giant branch; Karachentsev et al. 2003
images.discovered_by: James Dunlop

images.label: NGC 253 Sculptor Galaxy
images.distance_note: Tip of the red giant branch; Radburn-Smith et al. 2011
images.discovered_by: Caroline Herschel

images.label: NGC 253 Sculptor (wide field)
images.distance_note: ~3.5–3.7 Mpc: Rekola et al. 2005 PNLF 3.34 Mpc; TRGB 3.7–3.94 Mpc (Karachentsev et al. 2003; Anand et al. 2021 3.70 Mpc). Range 3.34–3.94 Mpc; TRGB best regarded
images.discovered_by: Caroline Herschel, 1783. Conventional credit: Caroline Herschel
images.description: Nearly edge-on SAB(s)c starburst spiral with intense nuclear star formation and a galactic superwind; brightest member of the Sculptor filament.

images.label: NGC 292 Small Magellanic Cloud
images.distance_note: Graczyk et al. 2020, ApJ 904, 13, D=62.44±0.47(stat)±0.81(syst) kpc (late-type eclipsing binaries)
images.discovered_by: Naked-eye object known since antiquity; first European written record by members of Magellan's expedition, 1519. No individual discovery credit
images.description: Low-metallicity irregular dwarf satellite galaxy of the Milky Way with active star formation and a line-of-sight depth of several kpc.

images.label: NGC 346 (SMC)
images.distance_note: Host galaxy SMC: Graczyk et al. 2020, ApJ 904, 13, 62.44 kpc (eclipsing binaries)
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1834–36 (Cape of Good Hope survey); catalogued in Dreyer's NGC 1888. Conventional credit: J. Herschel
images.description: Largest star-forming region in the SMC, an HII region and young cluster photoionised by a large population of hot OB stars including massive O-type members.

images.label: SMC core, NGC 346 region (HOO)
images.distance_note: Host galaxy SMC: Graczyk et al. 2020, ApJ 904, 13, 62.44 kpc (eclipsing binaries)
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1834–36 (Cape survey); NGC 1888
images.description: Field in the star-forming SMC bar around the OB cluster NGC 346; emission dominated by photoionised hydrogen and doubly-ionised oxygen.

images.label: NGC 474 Shell Galaxy
images.distance_note: Surface brightness fluctuation; ~32 Mpc. Estimates range 95-110 Mly
images.discovered_by: William Herschel
images.description: A lenticular galaxy in Pisces wrapped in faint concentric shells of stars. Those shells are the debris of smaller galaxies torn apart and absorbed, their stars still settling into the larger galaxy's gravity hundreds of millions of years later. NGC 474 is one of the clearest nearby examples of a galaxy built by mergers, and the shells are extremely faint - they need long broadband integration and very careful gradient control to show at all.

images.label: Comet 220P McNaught
images.constellation: Aries (transient — a comet's constellation changes with time and depends on the imaging epoch)
images.distance_note: Not applicable — Solar System body; light-year distance is not meaningful. Orbital elements (JPL/MPC): Jupiter-family comet in near-2:1 resonance with Jupiter, period ~5.5 yr, perihelion q≈1.6 AU (perihelion 14 June 2026), aphelion 4.679 AU (reached 12 March 2029)
images.discovered_by: Robert H. McNaught, 20 May 2004 (Siding Spring Survey, Uppsala Southern Schmidt Telescope, Siding Spring Observatory, NSW); announced as P/2004 K2 in IAU Circular 8348 (28 May 2004), confirmed by J. Young and A. Gilmore. Conventional credit: McNaught
images.description: Small icy Jupiter-family periodic comet; a sublimating cometary nucleus producing coma and tail near perihelion. Orbital period ~5.5 yr, perihelion ~1.6 AU, aphelion 4.68 AU.

images.label: NGC 1365 Great Barred Spiral
images.distance_note: ~18.1–18.6 Mpc: Hoyt et al. 2021 TRGB 18.1±0.5 Mpc; Madore et al./Silbermann et al. 1999 Cepheid 18.6±0.6 Mpc (Fornax Cluster). Midpoint ~18.3 Mpc; TRGB and Cepheid determinations agree
images.discovered_by: James Dunlop, 1826 (Parramatta, NSW). Conventional credit: Dunlop
images.description: Giant SBb barred spiral in the Fornax Cluster with a prominent bar, bar-fed star formation, and a Seyfert nucleus.

images.label: M45 Pleiades
images.distance_note: 136.2 pc from VLBI parallax; Melis et al. 2014, resolving the long-running disagreement with the Hipparcos value
images.discovered_by: Known since antiquity
images.description: An open cluster in Taurus, around 100 million years old and one of the nearest to the Sun. The blue haze around the brightest stars is not gas the cluster was born from but an unrelated dust cloud it happens to be drifting through, scattering starlight the way fog scatters a headlight. Its distance was disputed for two decades until radio interferometry settled it at about 444 light-years.

images.label: IC 2118 Witch Head
images.distance_note: ~210 pc (Kun et al. 2001); the illuminating star Rigel/β Orionis lies ~264 pc (Hipparcos/Gaia). Popular ~900 ly is a rough figure
images.discovered_by: William Herschel, 1786 (bright portion = NGC 1909); IC 2118 designation in Dreyer's Index Catalogue 1895. Conventional credit: W. Herschel
images.description: Cometary reflection nebula in the Orion–Eridanus superbubble; scatters light from the B8Ia supergiant Rigel (β Orionis). The centre coordinates fall in Eridanus, not Orion.

images.label: NGC 2018 (LMC)
images.distance_note: Host galaxy LMC: Pietrzyński et al. 2019, Nature 567, 200, 49.59±0.09(stat)±0.54(syst) kpc (eclipsing binaries)
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1834–36 (Cape survey); NGC 1888
images.description: Emission/HII complex in the Large Magellanic Cloud photoionised by embedded OB stars.

images.label: M1 Crab Nebula
images.discovered_by: John Bevis, 1731. The supernova itself was recorded by Chinese and Japanese astronomers in 1054
images.distance_note: ~2.0 kpc, conventional. NOT from the deep-research pass - verify.
images.description: The expanding remnant of the supernova of 1054, still growing at about 1,500 km/s. A pulsar at its centre spins 30 times a second and powers the nebula's synchrotron glow.

images.label: NGC 2070 Tarantula Nebula
images.distance_note: Host galaxy LMC: Pietrzyński et al. 2019, Nature 567, 200, 49.59 kpc (eclipsing binaries)
images.discovered_by: Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille, 1751–52 (Cape; originally catalogued as the 'star' 30 Doradus); NGC number from Dreyer 1888. Conventional credit: Lacaille
images.description: Largest and most active starburst HII region in the Local Group; central super star cluster NGC 2070 with core concentration R136 provides most of the ionising radiation — its dominant star R136a1 has a present-day mass of ~196 M☉ (range 169–230; Kalari et al. 2022), the most massive star known.

images.label: IC 434 Horsehead Nebula
images.discovered_by: Williamina Fleming, 1888, from a Harvard photographic plate
images.distance_note: ~400 pc to the L1630 / Orion B cloud (Gaia-era). Popularly quoted as 1,500 ly. NOT from the deep-research pass - verify.
images.description: A pillar of cold dust silhouetted against the emission ridge IC 434, lit from behind by sigma Orionis. The dark shape is Barnard 33; the frame also reaches the Flame Nebula, NGC 2024.

images.label: NGC 2174 Monkey Head Nebula
images.discovered_by: Karl Christian Bruhns, 1857
images.distance_note: ~2.0 kpc, conventional. NOT from the deep-research pass - verify.
images.description: An emission nebula and young cluster on the Orion-Gemini border, its pillars sculpted by radiation from the embedded OB stars.

images.label: NGC 2237 Rosette Nebula
images.discovered_by: Nebulosity: Lewis Swift, 1865 (NGC 2237). The central cluster NGC 2244 was seen by John Flamsteed around 1690
images.distance_note: ~1.6 kpc, conventional. NOT from the deep-research pass - verify.
images.description: A large emission nebula cleared into a ring by the winds and radiation of the young cluster NGC 2244 at its centre.

images.label: NGC 2264 Cone Nebula
images.distance_note: ~719–738 pc: Maíz Apellániz 2019 (Gaia DR2) 719±16 pc; Kuhn et al. 2019 738 pc (Mon OB1)
images.discovered_by: William Herschel, 1785 (Cone Nebula, H V.27); associated cluster 1784. Conventional credit: W. Herschel
images.description: Photoevaporating pillar of cold molecular gas in the Mon OB1 cloud, shaped by radiation from the O7 binary S Monocerotis in the adjacent Christmas Tree Cluster.

images.label: Sh2-308 Dolphin Head
images.distance_note: Distance to central star WR 6/EZ CMa (HD 50896) uncertain: Rate & Crowther 2020 (Gaia DR2) ~2.27 kpc (~7,400 ly); Gaia DR3 reductions ~1,537 pc (~5,010 ly); older 1,389–1,800 pc (4,530–5,870 ly), Hipparcos-2007 ~1,400 pc. Value shown ~1,900 pc is a midpoint of Gaia-era estimates; genuinely uncertain
images.discovered_by: Stewart Sharpless, 1959 (Sharpless catalogue Sh2-308; = RCW 11, LBN 1052)
images.description: Wolf–Rayet wind-blown bubble surrounding the WN4 star EZ Canis Majoris (WR 6/HD 50896); stellar-wind-swept shell photoionised by the star, prominent in doubly-ionised oxygen and X-ray-emitting.

images.label: IC 2177 Seagull Nebula
images.distance_note: ~1,120 pc via the ionising Be star HD 53367 (Gaia); commonly cited ~3,800 ly. NOTE: the supplied centre coordinate (Dec −11.11°) falls within Canis Major by IAU (Delporte 1930) boundaries, though the nebula straddles the Monoceros border
images.discovered_by: Isaac Roberts, 1898 (photographic); IC 2177 in Dreyer's Index Catalogue 1910. Conventional credit: Roberts
images.description: HII region on the Monoceros–Canis Major border centred on the Be star HD 53367 (B0IV/Ve); photoionised hydrogen forming the 'head', with Sh2-296 forming the 'wings'.

images.label: NGC 2359 Thor's Helmet
images.distance_note: Conventional ~3,670 pc (~11,960 ly). The Gaia DR2 parallax of WR 7/HD 56925 (0.210±0.027 mas) is low-precision (~15% error) and variously interpreted (implying ~4,800 pc); no consensus downward revision. Distance uncertain
images.discovered_by: William Herschel, 1785. Conventional credit: W. Herschel
images.description: Wind-blown bubble and bow-shock nebula around the WN4 Wolf–Rayet star WR 7 (HD 56925), shaped by the star's fast wind interacting with a molecular cloud and photoionised by its ultraviolet radiation.

images.label: NGC 2467 Skull and Crossbones
images.distance_note: Line-of-sight superposition — no single distance. HII region S311 ionised by O6 star HD 64315 (~4.1 kpc); superposed unrelated clusters Haffner 18 ~4.5 kpc (~14,700 ly) and Haffner 19 ~6.4 kpc (~20,900 ly), Vázquez et al. 2010. Value shown is for the S311/Haffner 18 component
images.discovered_by: William Herschel, 1784. Conventional credit: W. Herschel
images.description: Star-forming HII complex in Puppis; the S311 region is photoionised by the O6 star HD 64315, with several physically unrelated clusters projected along the same sight line at different distances.

images.label: Vela Supernova Remnant
images.distance_note: 287 pc (~936 ly) from Vela pulsar VLBI parallax 3.5±0.2 mas, Dodson et al. 2003, ApJ 596, 1137; cf. HST optical parallax 294 pc (Caraveo et al. 2001). Supersedes the older kinematic ~500 pc. Popular ~815 ly is too low
images.discovered_by: Vela pulsar (PSR B0833-45) discovered 1968 by Large, Vaughan & Mills (Molonglo, NSW); the SNR was mapped in 1950s–60s radio surveys. Conventional credit for the pulsar: Large et al. 1968
images.description: Evolved (~11,000 yr) supernova remnant with optical filaments from radiative shocks, powered at its heart by the Vela pulsar — a rotation-powered neutron star driving a synchrotron pulsar-wind nebula.

images.label: NGC 2736 Pencil Nebula
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1835 (Cape of Good Hope survey)
images.distance_note: 287 pc, from the Vela pulsar VLBI parallax (Dodson et al.). Same value as the Vela SNR entry - the Pencil is part of it.
images.description: A shock front within the Vela supernova remnant, where the blast wave is ploughing into a denser cloud. The thin bright filament is gas compressed and heated at the shock, moving at around 640,000 km/h.

images.label: NGC 3293 Gem Cluster
images.distance_note: ~2,335 pc (~7,600 ly): Dias et al. 2021 (Gaia DR2) 2,334±52 pc; Göppl & Preibisch 2022 (Gaia EDR3) ~2.3 kpc
images.discovered_by: Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille, 1751 (Cape; Lac). Conventional credit: Lacaille
images.description: Young, populous open cluster (~10–20 Myr) in the Carina complex containing many early-B stars plus blue and red supergiants (e.g. V361 Car); no O-type members remain.

images.label: NGC 3324 Gabriela Mistral
images.distance_note: ~2.3 kpc (~7,500 ly): Göppl & Preibisch 2022, Gaia EDR3 OB-star sample; adopted by the JWST Early Release Observations 2022. The popular ~9,100 ly (2,800 pc) is outdated
images.discovered_by: James Dunlop, 1826 (Parramatta, NSW). Conventional credit: Dunlop
images.description: HII region and young cluster on the north-west rim of the Carina Nebula, photoionised by O-type systems HD 92206 and CPD-57°3580; the eroded molecular wall is the JWST 'Cosmic Cliffs'.

images.label: NGC 3372 Carina Nebula
images.distance_note: 2.3 kpc (Smith 2006, expansion parallax of the η Carinae Homunculus)
images.discovered_by: Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille, 1751–52 (Cape). Conventional credit: Lacaille
images.description: Giant HII region and molecular cloud hosting clusters Trumpler 14 and Trumpler 16, about 70 O-type stars (Smith & Brooks 2010), the O2 supergiant HD 93129A, and the luminous blue variable η Carinae, which dominate its ionisation and wind energetics.

images.label: IC 2631 Chamaeleon Complex
images.distance_note: 192.7±0.4 pc (~629 ly), Gaia DR2 parallaxes to the Chamaeleon I North cloud, 2018; older ~160 pc (Whittet et al. 1997)
images.discovered_by: DeLisle Stewart, 1900 (photographic; = Cederblad 112); IC designation in Dreyer's Index Catalogue
images.description: Brightest reflection nebula in the Chamaeleon I cloud, illuminated by the Herbig Ae/Be pre-main-sequence star HD 97300 (B9V), which is ringed by an infrared dust bubble.

images.label: Gum 37 Tadpoles and Statue of Liberty (wide)
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1834-38 (Cape of Good Hope survey)
images.distance_note: ~2.35 kpc for NGC 3572 / Gum 37. NGC 3576 in the same frame is separately given as 9,100 ly, so this wide field spans both.
images.description: A wide field across the Carina arm taking in the Gum 37 tadpole globules around NGC 3572 and, in the same frame, the pillars of NGC 3576, the Statue of Liberty.

images.label: NGC 3572 Gum 37 Southern Tadpoles
images.distance_note: ~2.0–2.7 kpc: SIMBAD/VizieR ~2.0 kpc; Steppe 1977 (RGU photometry) 2.7 kpc. Midpoint ~2.35 kpc (~7,600 ly); range 6,500–8,800 ly
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1834 (Cape). Conventional credit: J. Herschel
images.description: Open cluster with associated HII region Gum 37 (RCW 54) in the Carina spiral feature; contains photoevaporating cometary globules ('tadpoles') shaped by cluster OB radiation.

images.label: NGC 3572 / Gum 37
images.distance_note: ~2.0–2.7 kpc: SIMBAD ~2.0 kpc; Steppe 1977 2.7 kpc. Midpoint ~2.35 kpc; range 6,500–8,800 ly
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1834 (Cape). Conventional credit: J. Herschel
images.description: Open cluster with associated HII region Gum 37 (RCW 54) in the Carina spiral feature; contains photoevaporating cometary globules shaped by cluster OB radiation.

images.label: NGC 3576 Statue of Liberty
images.distance_note: ~2.4–3.0 kpc: Persi et al. 1994 ~2.4 kpc; Damineli et al. 2002 ~2.8 kpc. Value ~2.8 kpc (~9,100 ly)
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1834 (Cape). Conventional credit: J. Herschel
images.description: Compact HII region (RCW 57A, Gum 38a) with active massive-star formation, PAH emission, and embedded OB stars; physically in front of the more distant giant cluster NGC 3603.

images.label: NGC 3628 Hamburger Galaxy
images.discovered_by: William Herschel, 1784
images.distance_note: ~10.7 Mpc. NOT from the deep-research pass - verify.
images.description: An edge-on spiral with a thick, warped dust lane cutting its length. The faintest member of the Leo Triplet with M65 and M66, and tidally distorted by them.

images.label: IC 2944 Running Chicken
images.distance_note: ~2,331 pc (~7,600 ly), Gaia DR3 (Reipurth et al. 2025) to the OB subgroup; older popular ~6,500 ly (2,000 pc)
images.discovered_by: Nebula (IC 2944/2948): Royal H. Frost, 1904 (Bruce telescope, Arequipa); Thackeray's globules: A. D. Thackeray, 1950. Conventional credit for nebula: Frost
images.description: HII region and open cluster (Collinder 249) around λ Centauri, photoionised by cluster O-stars (e.g. HD 101205), containing the dark Bok globules known as Thackeray's globules.

images.label: NGC 4038 Antennae Galaxies
images.distance_note: 22±3 Mpc (Schweizer et al. 2008, AJ 136, 1482, from Type Ia SN 2007sr and a revised TRGB 20.0 Mpc, plus a flow model 22.5 Mpc). This supersedes the short 13.3 Mpc TRGB of Saviane et al. 2008, attributed to a TRGB misidentification. Best regarded: 22 Mpc
images.discovered_by: William Herschel, 1785. Conventional credit: W. Herschel
images.description: Prototypical major merger of two gas-rich spirals with long tidal tails and intense, cluster-forming starbursts triggered along the collision interface.

images.label: Sandqvist 149 Dark Doodad
images.distance_note: Musca molecular cloud from Gaia 3D dust: Zucker et al. 2021 ~171–173 pc; Musca filament ~140–150 pc (Franco 1991; Cox et al. 2016). Range ~140–190 pc; midpoint ~165 pc (~538 ly). Supersedes older ~700 ly figures
images.discovered_by: Aage Sandqvist, 1977 (Stockholm Observatory; dark-cloud catalogue, from ESO(B) Schmidt plates); nickname 'Dark Doodad' coined by Dennis di Cicco, 1986
images.description: Long, narrow filamentary dark absorption nebula in the Musca molecular cloud; dense dust extinguishing background starlight, with no significant internal illumination.

images.label: M104 Sombrero Galaxy
images.distance_note: 9.55±0.13(stat)±0.31(syst) Mpc (McQuinn et al. 2016, AJ 152, 144, HST TRGB); consistent with SBF ~9.1 Mpc
images.discovered_by: Pierre Méchain, 1781; added to Messier's catalogue (M104) later. Conventional credit: Méchain
images.description: Massive edge-on Sa spiral with a large bulge, a prominent equatorial dust lane, an extensive globular cluster system (~2,000), and a supermassive-black-hole nucleus.

images.label: NGC 5128 Centaurus A
images.distance_note: 3.8±0.1 Mpc (Harris, Rejkuba & Harris 2010, PASA 27, 457 — best-estimate mean of Cepheid, TRGB, PNLF, SBF and Mira methods)
images.discovered_by: James Dunlop, 1826 (Parramatta, NSW). Conventional credit: Dunlop
images.description: Nearest giant elliptical galaxy, a recent merger with a warped central dust lane, powered by an active galactic nucleus driving relativistic synchrotron radio jets.

images.label: M83 Southern Pinwheel
images.distance_note: ~4.5–4.9 Mpc: Thim et al. 2003 Cepheid 4.5 Mpc (μ=28.32); Karachentsev et al. 2007 TRGB ~4.9 Mpc (μ=28.56). Midpoint ~4.6 Mpc
images.discovered_by: Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille, 1752 (Cape); added to Messier's catalogue (M83) 1781. Conventional credit: Lacaille
images.description: Nearby barred grand-design starburst spiral (SAB(s)c) with a high supernova rate and vigorous bar-fed nuclear star formation.

images.label: NGC 5367 / CG 12
images.distance_note: ~630 pc (Williams et al. 1977); alternative ~550 pc (Maheswar et al.). No clean modern Gaia DR3 determination located; range ~550–630 pc. Value shown ~630 pc ≈ 2,050 ly. Amateur ~2,500 ly figures are not well supported
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1834 (nebula NGC 5367); the cometary globule CG 12 was catalogued by Hawarden & Brand, 1976. Conventional credit for NGC 5367: J. Herschel
images.description: High-galactic-latitude cometary globule hosting reflection nebula NGC 5367, illuminated by the early-B binary h4636; a rare site of intermediate-mass star formation far from the Galactic plane.

images.label: Barnard 228 Dark Wolf
images.distance_note: ~155 pc (~505 ly), Lupus 1 cloud: Galli et al. 2020 (Gaia DR2) 150–160 pc; Zucker et al. 2021 ~155 pc. Popular ~500 ly is coincidentally close
images.discovered_by: E. E. Barnard (Barnard Catalogue of 349 Dark Objects, published 1927). Conventional credit: Barnard
images.description: Elongated dark absorption nebula in the Lupus 1 molecular cloud, one of the nearest low-mass star-forming regions; opaque dust silhouetted against the background star field.

images.label: IC 4601 Blue Reflection
images.distance_note: Part of the Rho Ophiuchi / Upper Scorpius complex; Gaia distances to the association cluster near 140 pc
images.discovered_by: Edward Emerson Barnard
images.description: A reflection nebula on the northern edge of the Rho Ophiuchi complex, one of the closest star-forming regions to the Sun. There is no emission here - the colour is starlight scattered off dust, and dust scatters blue more efficiently than red, which is why reflection nebulae are cold in tone while emission nebulae are red. Dark lanes threading the field are denser parts of the same cloud blocking the stars behind.

images.label: LDN 1688 Rho Ophiuchi Complex
images.distance_note: 137.3±1.2 pc (~448 ly), Ortiz-León et al. 2017 (VLBA trigonometric parallaxes); confirmed by Gaia DR2 138.4±2.6 pc (Ortiz-León et al. 2018)
images.discovered_by: Beverly T. Lynds, 1962 (Lynds Dark Nebulae catalogue, from POSS plates). Conventional credit: Lynds
images.description: Dense core of the nearest low-mass star-forming complex, rich in embedded protostars and prestellar cores; associated reflection nebulosity is lit by nearby B-type stars.

images.label: NGC 6164 Dragon's Egg
images.distance_note: ~1.1 kpc (~3,600 ly) to the central star HD 148937 (Gaia DR3 offset-corrected parallax, cited Lim et al. 2024); older estimates 4,000–6,000 ly
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1834 (NGC 6164); the symmetric bipolar structure was recognised by Karl Henize, 1959. Conventional credit for NGC 6164: J. Herschel
images.description: Rare bipolar ejecta nebula around the magnetic Of?p O-type star HD 148937; symmetric lobes of stellar-ejected, photoionised gas within a wind-blown shell and Strömgren sphere, likely the product of a stellar merger.

images.label: LDN 43 Cosmic Bat
images.distance_note: ~1,400 ly (~430 pc; APOD, Constellation Guide). [UNVERIFIED against a primary source — some studies of associated young stars (RNO 90/91) imply a nearer ~125–140 pc; the two figures are in tension. Constellation confirmed as Ophiuchus from the coordinates]
images.discovered_by: Beverly T. Lynds, 1962 (Lynds Dark Nebulae catalogue). Conventional credit: Lynds
images.description: Dark Bok-globule filament and dense molecular cloud harbouring young stellar objects; obscuring dust with embedded protostars driving outflows and small cometary reflection nebulae.

images.label: NGC 6188 Fighting Dragons (SHO)
images.distance_note: ~1.3 kpc (~4,300 ly): Arnal et al. 2003; Ara OB1a ~1,320–1,380 pc (Humphreys). Consistent with popular ~4,000 ly
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1836 (Rim Nebula NGC 6188); the ionising cluster NGC 6193 was recorded by James Dunlop, 1826. Conventional credit for NGC 6188: J. Herschel
images.description: Bright-rimmed HII region (RCW 108, Gum 53) in Ara OB1, photoionised by the cluster NGC 6193 — chiefly the O-star systems HD 150136 and HD 150135.

images.label: NGC 6188 Fighting Dragons (HOO)
images.distance_note: ~1.3 kpc (~4,300 ly): Arnal et al. 2003; Ara OB1a ~1,320–1,380 pc
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1836 (Rim Nebula); cluster NGC 6193 by James Dunlop, 1826. Conventional credit for NGC 6188: J. Herschel
images.description: Bright-rimmed HII region (RCW 108, Gum 53) in Ara OB1, photoionised by the cluster NGC 6193, chiefly the O-star systems HD 150136 and HD 150135.

images.label: SL 17 Fenrir (Sandqvist 17)
images.distance_note: Distance via associated RCW 113/Gum 55 and Sco OB1: NGC 6231 ~1,640 pc (Sana et al. 2008) to Sco OB1 ~1,910 pc (Humphreys); range 5,300–6,200 ly, midpoint ~1,775 pc. Genuinely uncertain
images.discovered_by: Aage Sandqvist & Kjell Lindroos, 1976 (catalogued in Sandqvist 1977, from ESO(B) Schmidt plates)
images.description: Dark absorption nebula silhouetted against the emission nebula RCW 113 / Gum 55, which surrounds the Sco OB1 association and its core cluster NGC 6231.

images.label: IC 4628 Prawn Nebula
images.distance_note: ~1,640 pc (~5,350 ly) via NGC 6231/Sco OB1 (Sana et al. 2008); popular ~6,000 ly
images.discovered_by: E. E. Barnard, ~1900 (photographic); IC designation in Dreyer's Index Catalogue. Conventional credit: Barnard
images.description: Large HII emission nebula (Gum 56) in the Sagittarius Arm, photoionised by O-stars of the Sco OB1 association and the cluster NGC 6231.

images.label: IC 4633 and the Apus IFN
images.distance_note: IC 4633 itself; the integrated flux nebula in front of it lies only a few hundred light-years away, inside our own galaxy
images.discovered_by: DeLisle Stewart
images.description: A face-on spiral galaxy in Apus seen through a curtain of integrated flux nebula - dust in our own galaxy's halo, far above the plane, glowing faintly from the combined light of every star in the Milky Way. The two sit at wildly different distances: the dust is a few hundred light-years away, the galaxy around a hundred million. IFN is among the faintest structure amateur equipment can record.

images.label: NGC 6334 Cat's Paw Nebula
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1837 (Cape of Good Hope survey)
images.distance_note: 1.34 kpc from VLBI water-maser parallax, Chibueze et al. 2014. Older literature commonly says 5,500 ly. NOT from the deep-research pass - verify.
images.description: A giant star-forming complex whose bright emission knots form the toe-pads of the 'paw'. One of the most active regions of massive star formation within 2 kpc of the Sun.

images.label: NGC 6357 Lobster Nebula
images.distance_note: ~1.7 kpc (~5,500 ly), professional Gaia/spectroscopic value (SIMBAD 1,800±140 pc; Russeil, Reid). The popular ~8,000 ly (2.4 kpc) is overstated
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1837 (Cape). Conventional credit: J. Herschel
images.description: Giant HII complex (Sh2-11, RCW 131) whose central open cluster Pismis 24 hosts several of the most massive known O-stars (e.g. the Pismis 24-1 system), which dominate its ionisation.

images.label: M20 Trifid Nebula
images.distance_note: ~1,180 pc (~3,850 ly), Kuhn et al. 2019/2021 (Gaia); older estimates 1.67 kpc and the 4,100–5,200 ly range are now superseded by Gaia astrometry
images.discovered_by: Charles Messier, 1764 (catalogued as M20; = NGC 6514). Conventional credit: Messier
images.description: Young HII region photoionised by the O7.5V star HD 164492A, trisected by dust lanes, with an adjoining blue reflection component to the north.

images.label: M8 Lagoon Nebula
images.distance_note: ~1,250 pc (~4,080 ly), Damiani et al. 2017 (Gaia distance to the embedded cluster NGC 6530); consistent with the current guess
images.discovered_by: Cluster NGC 6530 noted by John Flamsteed c.1680; nebula recorded by Giovanni Hodierna before 1654 and catalogued by Charles Messier, 1764 (M8). Conventional credit: Messier
images.description: Giant HII region and cluster NGC 6530, photoionised mainly by the O4 star 9 Sagittarii, with the compact Hourglass sub-region ionised by Herschel 36 (O7.5V).

images.label: M8 Lagoon to NGC 6559 Chinese Dragon (wide)
images.discovered_by: M8: Giovanni Battista Hodierna, before 1654. NGC 6559: John Herschel, 1837
images.distance_note: ~1,250 pc, Damiani et al. 2017 (Gaia). Matches the separate M8 and NGC 6559 entries - one physical complex.
images.description: A wide field spanning the whole Sagittarius complex, from the Lagoon Nebula across to the dust and emission of NGC 6559. Both lie at the same distance in the same star-forming cloud.

images.label: NGC 6559 Chinese Dragon
images.distance_note: ~1,250 pc (~4,080 ly), physically part of the M8/Lagoon complex (Gaia); popular ~5,000 ly. Range 4,100–5,000 ly
images.discovered_by: John Herschel, 1837 (Cape). Conventional credit: J. Herschel
images.description: Small combined emission and reflection nebula with active star formation east of the Lagoon, lit by young embedded stars amid dark dust lanes.

images.label: Sh2-68 Flaming Skull
images.distance_note: PN G030.6+06.2. Distance poorly constrained; published values span roughly 1,000-2,300 ly
images.discovered_by: Stewart Sharpless
images.description: A planetary nebula in Serpens, the shed envelope of a dying Sun-like star. Its central white dwarf is moving fast enough through the interstellar medium that the nebula is being left behind and distorted, which is why it looks lopsided rather than like a neat ring. It is extremely faint in both hydrogen and oxygen, so it rewards restraint in processing rather than an aggressive stretch.

images.label: NGC 6726 Anteater / R CrA
images.distance_note: 149 pc (~486 ly), Galli et al. 2020 (Gaia DR2); Zucker et al. 2020 151 pc. Supersedes the older ~130 pc (425 ly) kinematic value
images.discovered_by: Johann F. J. Schmidt, 1861 (NGC 6726/6727). Conventional credit: Schmidt
images.description: Reflection nebulae NGC 6726/6727 in the Corona Australis molecular cloud, scattering light from the young stars TY CrA and HD 176386; part of one of the nearest star-forming regions.

images.label: NGC 6729 Corona Australis
images.distance_note: 149 pc (~486 ly), Galli et al. 2020 (Gaia DR2); Zucker et al. 2020 151 pc
images.discovered_by: Johann F. J. Schmidt, 1861 (variable nebula); independently noted by Albert Marth, 1864. Conventional credit: Schmidt
images.description: Fan-shaped variable reflection/emission nebula opening from the Herbig pre-main-sequence star R CrA toward T CrA within the Corona Australis molecular cloud.

images.label: NGC 6744 Pavo Galaxy
images.distance_note: 9.01±0.38 Mpc (Anand et al. 2021, PHANGS-HST TRGB); NED redshift-independent mean ~7.2 Mpc. TRGB best regarded
images.discovered_by: James Dunlop, 1826 (Parramatta, NSW). Conventional credit: Dunlop
images.description: Large intermediate-type barred spiral (SAB(r)bc) with a flocculent, extended disc, often described as a Milky Way analogue.

images.label: Eagle Ray Nebula
images.distance_note: Tentative ~215 pc (~700 ly) from association with a high-latitude molecular cloud in the Aquila Rift (Magnani et al. 1985). [UNVERIFIED — the identification with Sh2-63/LBN 82 and this distance could not be confirmed against a primary catalogue entry this session; treat as provisional]
images.discovered_by: Stewart Sharpless, 1959 (Sharpless catalogue, as Sh2-63/LBN 82). [Identification UNVERIFIED]
images.description: High-galactic-latitude faint nebula; the supplied coordinates (19h57.7m, −14°07′) fall within Sagittarius by IAU boundaries (not Aquila or Aquarius), in a region associated with the Aquila Rift complex.

images.label: NGC 6960 Veil Nebula
images.distance_note: 725±15 pc (~2,360 ly), Fesen et al. 2021, MNRAS 507, 244 (Gaia EDR3 parallaxes of stars in/behind the Cygnus Loop). Verified
images.discovered_by: William Herschel, 1784. Conventional credit: W. Herschel
images.description: Western filament ('Witch's Broom') of the Cygnus Loop, a middle-aged (~10–20 kyr) supernova remnant emitting via radiative shock excitation as the blast wave sweeps the interstellar medium; 52 Cygni is an unrelated foreground star.

images.label: NGC 7293 Helix Nebula
images.distance_note: ~200 pc (655±13 ly), Gaia EDR3 parallax (~5.01 mas) of the central white dwarf WD 2226-210 (Gaia Collaboration 2021)
images.discovered_by: Karl Ludwig Harding, before 1824. Conventional credit: Harding
images.description: One of the nearest planetary nebulae; an expelled AGB envelope photoionised by the ~120,000 K white-dwarf central star, featuring radial cometary knots with ionised tails pointing away from the star.

images.label: NGC 7582 Grus Quartet
images.distance_note: ~20.6 Mpc for NGC 7582 (Grus Quartet flow-model distances span 18.3–22.5 Mpc); redshift-independent ~21 Mpc. Midpoint ~20.4 Mpc
images.discovered_by: James Dunlop, 1826 (Parramatta, NSW; discovered together with NGC 7552). Conventional credit: Dunlop
images.description: Barred spiral Seyfert 2 galaxy with a circumnuclear starburst ring and gas outflow; brightest member of the interacting Grus Quartet — together with NGC 7552, NGC 7590 and NGC 7599 — whose members are linked by tidal HI, indicating ongoing gravitational interaction.
